messages:
Morgan: Quick sync — prepping UAT POC with AcmeCorp. They need SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC by tenant. Main asks: domain proof for tenant isolation, sample SAML attribute mapping, SCIM rate/partial-sync behavior, and a ballpark for Dedicated capacity pricing during a 4-week POC. Also any blockers from security/legal?
Lee: Got it. For SAML we can provide metadata XML and an attribute map example. Do we need nameID:email or persistent?
Morgan: Customer prefers email as NameID. They want groups -> roles mapping (admins, editors, viewers).
Lee: Ok. Example mapping I usually send:
```
<NameIDFormat>urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress</NameIDFormat>
<Attribute name="groups">memberOf</Attribute>
```
Will attach complete metadata. SCIM: we support full user + group sync, delta sync via /Users?filter=lastModified gt ... and bulk via pagination. Typical rate limits 100 req/min per org during POC unless we raise.
Anita: Security notes: SCIM service account should be scoped to users and groups only. We recommend provisioning with least privilege and scoped tokens. Also we log provisioning events to audit logs for 90 days by default. Any need for longer retention?
Morgan: Legal asked about audit retention — they need 1 year for this POC. Is that doable?
Anita: For a short POC we can retain exports on request, but long-term retention requires add-on. I'll flag to compliance.
Alex: Networking: For Private/Dedicated POC we can spin a VPC peering connection or use customer-hosted tunnel. If they want on-prem access, we need IP allowlist + hostname proofing. For tenant isolation we verify domain control via DNS TXT record or email proof to a domain admin.
Lee: For RBAC model: we support role templates + custom role mapping from SAML groups and SCIM group membership. Can do canister-level isolation (per-tenant resources) or org-level with role filters. Which does Acme want?
Morgan: They want per-tenant resource isolation (separate tenant IDs) plus cross-tenant admin audit.
Lee: That’s fine — will outline rollout steps: 1) exchange SAML metadata, 2) set up SCIM service account + test user import, 3) map groups->roles, 4) verify domain proof (DNS TXT), 5) enable POC Dedicated capacity and smoke test.
Tom: From legal: we'll need completed security questionnaire (AICPA app or custom), SOC2 snapshot, and a standard DPA for the POC. Also confirm data residency — EU or US?
Morgan: Customer needs EU data residency for the POC.
Anita: EU residency ok — we can pin the POC to eu-west region. Note: if using Dedicated GPUs in eu-west, cost is higher.
Lee: Pricing rough: Dedicated POC baseline (1 x A100-equivalent pool) about ~$XXk/month prorated — for 4 weeks we can give a trial discount. I’ll follow up with a written quote.
Morgan: Can we offer a temporary uplift to rate limits for SCIM during initial import? They have ~15k users.
Alex: Yes — bumping to 500 req/min for a 24h import window is possible with engineering signoff. Need ETA for user CSV and peak concurrency.
Lee: One more technical edge case: group nesting — Acme uses nested groups in IDP. We can flatten on import but we need to know depth. Please ask them for an example payload.
Morgan: Asking customer for IDP export + one sample user, group hierarchy, and preferred NameID. They’ll also send their security questionnaire.
Tom: I’ll prep standard DPA + addendum for one-month POC and EU processing clause.
Anita: Security checklist items I need answered: 1) SCIM service account owner email, 2) MFA requirement for admins, 3) IP ranges for SAML metadata callback if any. Also want pen-test window if they request deeper testing.
Lee: I’ll draft the SAML/SCIM playbook and include sample attribute map + a quick curl SCIM import example.
Morgan: Awesome — can we try to have metadata + SCIM creds by EOD tomorrow so we can start imports Thursday?
deploy-bot: Documentation: https://docs.redwood.ai/poc/sso-scim-tenant-isolation (shared) :link:
Lee: Thanks — I’ll attach the sample payload and the pricing note after this thread.
Morgan: Perfect. I’ll confirm timeline with customer and post updates here. :thumbsup:
